title: A Shorter Way for a Bee
paragraphs: Can a bee find a better way to finish a task after watching another bee? A team at Queen Mary University of London explored this question with small balls. In their experiment, bumblebees could get food by moving a ball to the middle of a platform.

Some bees watched a trained bee do the job before trying it themselves. The trained bee moved the ball that was furthest from the middle. Later, the watching bees had a choice of three balls at different distances. They often chose the nearest one, so they had less distance to move it.

Choosing a different ball made their solution more efficient. The result suggests that these bees could change what they had learned to suit a new situation. Learning here was more than repeating the same actions.
